chapter_title: Concerning the Five Forms that exist in the Rulers
spiritual_reading:
# Spiritual Translation: The Ruling Love of the Selfhood and Its Five Genera of Evil

---

**¶1:** Consider the ruling love of self, which governs all the affections of evil and falsity. Now, five genera of evil constitute its whole selfhood, answering to the five fundamental kinds of evil that exist within the five realms of opposition to the Divine.

**¶2:** Indeed, its governing principle is the lust for dominion, which originates from self-love. Its power of thought and capacity for elevation are the pride of self-derived intelligence, formed after the pattern of those who dwell in vain reasoning and persuasive falsity. Its power to act and its natural life are evil affections themselves, formed after the pattern of those who dwell in the obscurity that arises from evil. Its interior appetite is the falsification of truth, formed after the pattern of the realm of pure falsity from evil. Its lowest and most external expression is sensory falsity, which belongs to the realm of those who live in perverted knowledges. These five genera of evil constitute its selfhood, and they originate from the five fundamental kinds of evil within the five realms of opposition to the Divine.

**¶3:** When it wills, it shall proceed in its natural life [GAP-1] the realm of obscurity from evil. Also, when it wills, it shall [GAP-2] by the fourfold [GAP-3] through its power to act and its natural life [GAP-4] like those who live from self-love. When it wills, it shall elevate itself through pride of self-intelligence, like those who dwell in vain reasoning. Also, when it wills, it shall plunge down into falsities, like those who live in perverted knowledges. Again, when it wills, it shall move wholly from its lowest appetite, like those who dwell in pure falsity from evil. These five genera of evil constitute its selfhood.

**¶4:** Also, there are three further capacities within it.

**¶5:** The first: [GAP-5] its evil affections [GAP-6]

**¶6:** The second concerns the art of persuasive falsity. When it wills, it [GAP-7] its arts of deception. When it wills, it shall invoke concealment upon itself and hide its nature from the very evil affections it governs. When it wills, it shall manifest itself to them and destroy spiritual life through its arts of deception. Whatever falsity it may propagate at that moment, it shall [GAP-8: REVIEW — exercise deceptive persuasion] through it.

**¶7:** The third: Its selfhood is impenetrable, a[GAP-9: 1] [GAP-10] — the outermost expressions and instruments of its evil affections are unable to breach it. No hardened natural truth nor any appearance of natural good shall equal it [GAP-11]; they shall not be able to destroy it, because it was constituted and formed from the unyielding will of pure evil, the origin of all evil affections and all falsities.

**¶8:** Again, there are three further capacities within it.

**¶9:** When it wills, its self-love shall blaze forth, and its entire selfhood shall be made wholly into the [GAP-12: consuming intensity of] self-love.

**¶10:** Also, when it wills, it shall send forth the absence of all charity, and its entire selfhood freezes into a [GAP-13: lifeless mass of] cold indifference.

**¶11:** The third: Whenever its evil affections stand present before it, it shall perceive them and understand; for [whatever ex]ists in their will it shall comprehend — what is in their will and their manifest expression, so long as they are present before it. When they withdraw from its presence and separate themselves from it, it shall not comprehend what is in their will. There is no spiritual life in it whatsoever, but its semblance of 'life' is the bitterness of wrath that is manifest upon its countenance and in the terror it inspires. When a [GAP-14] devastation that is establ[ished be]fore it.

---

## Translator's Note

The entire chapter describes the anatomy of the *proprium* — the selfhood in its fullest infernal form — as a composite of five genera of evil: *self-love as dominion* (fire/lion), *pride of self-intelligence* (wind/eagle), *evil affections in act* (smoke/daemons), *falsity destroying truth from within* (darkness/dragon), and *sensory falsity at the lowest natural level* (water/fish). The three additional capacities in ¶4–7 describe how this selfhood operates: through its affections, through persuasive deception, and through imperviousness to destruction. The three in ¶8–11 describe its states: the inflammation of self-love, the freezing absence of charity, and a limited perception that functions only in the presence of its own evils — confirming that there is no genuine life in it, only the reactive semblance of life through wrath and the desire to dominate through fear. This corresponds precisely to Swedenborg's teaching that the proprium, regarded in itself, is nothing but evil, and that the hells have no life of their own, but only a counterfeit life animated by the fire of self-love and the cold of contempt for others.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: Consider the ruler, the leader of all the powers of darkness. Now, five forms exist in his body, corresponding to (the archetype) of the five creations that exist in the five worlds of darkness.

Indeed, his head is lion-faced, which came about from the world of fire. His wings and his shoulders are eagle-faced, after the likeness of the children of the wind. His hands and his feet are daemons, after the likeness of the children of the world of smoke. His belly is dragon-faced, after the likeness of the world of darkness. His tail is the form of the fish, which belongs to the world of the children of water. These five shapes are in him, and they came from the five creations of the five worlds of darkness.

Should he wish, he shall walk on his two feet [like the children of the] world of smoke. Also, when he wants, he shall [go upon] four [feet] on his hands and feet [and run] like the children of fire. Should he wish, he shall rise up on his wings, like the children of the wind. Also, should he wish, he shall plunge down to the waters like the children of water. Again, should he wish, he shall crawl on his belly like the children of darkness. These five shapes are in him.
Also, there are three other (qualities) in him.
The first: [He is lord over] his powers [and they obey him]

The second: Shall a [creature withstand] his magic arts. When he wishes, he shall make an invocation over himself, and hide from his powers. When he wants, he shall show himself to them and strike a death-blow by his magic arts. Any word he might utter at that moment, he shall [wreak magic] by it.

The third: His body is strong, a[nd] [the] nails and claws of his powers are not able to penetrate it. No iron nor copper body will equal him [in strength]; they will not be able to destroy him, because he was formed and fashioned from the hard-hearted counsel of Matter, the mother of demons and fiends.
Again, there are three others in him.
When he wants, his fire shall {blaze), and his entire body be made like the [flame of] fire.
Also, when he wishes, he shall send out frost, and his entire body freezes like a [mountain of] snow.

The third: Whenever his powers are stood before him, he shall look at them and understand; for [whatever ex]ists in their heart he shall understand, what is in their heart and their face so long as they are stood before him. When they retreat before him and distance themselves from him, he shall not understand what is in their heart. There is no life in him whatsoever, but his 'life' is the bile of anger that is apparent on his face and in his fear. Shall a [creature escape the] destruction that is establ[ished be]fore him.

fills.explanation: Every other movement comparison in ¶3 follows the pattern "like the children of X," and ¶2 uses the exact phrase "the children of the world of smoke," so this gap must supply the identical comparative formula before "world of smoke."

The passage lists five modes of locomotion (walk, fly, plunge, crawl); the fire/lion mode requires a verb for quadrupedal movement on all fours, and "go upon" naturally introduces "four feet" as a quadruped gait.

The numeral "four" requires a body-part noun to form the quadruped image, and "feet" is immediately glossed by the clarifying phrase "on his hands and feet" that follows, confirming "four feet" as the intended expression.

Each of the five modes pairs a specific dynamic verb with its corresponding world; the lion/fire movement is running, and "and run" provides the characteristic verb of the fire-world creatures to complete the comparison.

The first of three capacities must describe dominion — the ruling love's authority over its subordinate evil affections — and "He is lord over his powers" expresses the Ruler's supremacy in the Kephalaia's register.

The first quality — dominion over subordinate powers — is naturally completed by a statement of the powers' subjection, corresponding to the Swedenborgian principle that the ruling love commands all its subordinate affections.

The construction "Shall a [GAP-7] his magic arts" is a rhetorical question paralleling GAP-14, and the following description shows that no subordinate being can resist his deception — "creature withstand" supplies the subject and verb for this challenge.

The editor's reading "wreak magic" accurately expresses the spiritual sense of exercising deceptive power through utterance; the verb "wreak" conveys the active infliction of magical force consistent with the Kephalaia's cosmological register.
The visible letter "a" plus the missing character(s) must form a conjunction linking "His body is strong" to the clause about nails and claws; "and" is the only grammatically natural connector here.
After "and," the definite article "the" is required to introduce the noun phrase "the nails and claws of his powers," completing the grammatically necessary construction.

The comparison "No iron nor copper body will equal him" requires a quality of comparison, and "in strength" completes the clause by specifying the dimension of the ruler's unmatched bodily imperviousness.

"Flame of fire" is the standard ancient cosmological and biblical expression (cf. Exodus 3:2, Revelation 1:14) for the consuming manifestation of fire, corresponding to the spiritual sense of the blazing intensity of self-love.

The image of freezing requires a massive, lifeless object for comparison; "mountain of snow" is the standard ancient cosmological image for an inert frozen mass, expressing the total absence of charity's warmth.

Paralleling the rhetorical question in GAP-7 ("Shall a creature withstand his magic arts"), this closing formula asks whether any being can escape the devastation established before the ruler, completing the chapter's portrait of the proprium's inescapable destructiveness.
